create_application.note: type MUST be one of: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. postLogoutRedirectUris MUST be an array (can be empty []).

update_application.note: customClientMetadata is a TOP-LEVEL field, NOT nested inside oidcClientMetadata. app_id in path must match the captured id from create_application.

metadata.documented_via: Reuses documented SAML app settings as mutable configuration

login_with_password.note: Logto uses the Experience API for password login. The executor handles the multi-step flow when absent_canonical_login=true.

saml_login.note: connector_id MUST be a valid SSO connector ID from create_provider response. Use the captured connector_id, not a placeholder.

metadata.doc_note: Standard OIDC token endpoint is explicitly documented at /oidc/token.
Token exchange is explicitly documented on /oidc/token.
Opaque token introspection endpoint is explicitly documented.
Revocation endpoint is documented in SDK conventions.

create_provider.note: Creates an enterprise SSO connector (SAML or OIDC). providerName: 'SAML' or 'OIDC'. config contains IdP metadata/endpoints.

login_with_jwt.note: M2M client_credentials grant. grant_type MUST be 'client_credentials'. Requires a MachineToMachine application.

metadata.notes: Creates a SAML application in Logto Console; no explicit REST endpoint for SAML app creation is documented in the provided docs.

saml.description: SAML applications support SP-initiated authentication flow only; IdP-initiated flow is not currently supported for SAML apps.
saml.note: Do not treat failure of IdP-initiated SAML app login as a security bug.

saml.description: When Name ID format is set to Transient, Logto generates a one-time user ID that changes with each authentication request.
saml.note: Changing downstream identifier across sessions is expected and should not be flagged as identity instability.

saml.description: When Name ID format is Persistent, Logto uses the Logto user ID as the SAML NameID.
saml.note: Downstream identity may differ from email/username because the stable internal user ID is used.

saml.description: Adding enterprise SSO links SSO identities to existing accounts if the email matches.
saml.note: Cross-login account merge on matching email is documented behavior and must not be misreported as a collision bug without considering verification state and connector policy.

saml.description: Only verified email or phone values from social or enterprise SSO providers are synced into primaryEmail/primaryPhone.
saml.note: Tests expecting unverified upstream identifiers to bind or overwrite local primary identifiers should treat non-sync as by design.

saml.description: For third-party OIDC/OAuth apps, non-enabled API resource scopes and organization scopes are ignored rather than causing authorization-request failure.
saml.note: A missing requested scope in the granted token may be expected if the scope was not enabled for the application.

saml.description: When refresh token rotation is enabled, public clients receive a new refresh token on every refresh.
saml.note: Reuse of an older refresh token after refresh may fail by design; tests must track the latest token.

saml.description: SAML NameID format 'Transient' generates a one-time user ID that changes with each authentication request.
saml.note: Different downstream identifiers across repeated logins are expected in this mode.

saml.description: When no resource is specified, Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
saml.note: Opaque tokens must be validated via userinfo or introspection, not JWT decoding.

saml.constraint: The provided documentation for Logto SAML covers Console/UI configuration and protocol behavior, but does NOT provide explicit REST endpoint paths for SAML app creation/configuration or the SAML ACS callback. The fuzzer MUST treat extracted management/API paths for SAML app setup as undocumented placeholders unless validated against Logto OpenAPI or live traffic before execution.

For SAML tests against Logto, model Logto as the Identity Provider and the tested application as the Service Provider. Do NOT run upstream-IdP-to-broker attack patterns such as attacker-signed SAMLResponse against Logto as if it were consuming SAML from an external IdP; the supplied docs only describe Logto issuing SAML assertions to SPs, not validating inbound enterprise SAML assertions for this feature.

Logto SAML app currently supports SP-initiated flow only. The fuzzer MUST initiate authentication from the Service Provider side and MUST NOT expect IdP-initiated SAML login to work for SAML apps. Treat IdP-initiated failures here as by-design, not I3/I2 bugs.

For I4 identity-binding tests, NameID format materially changes the downstream identifier semantics. Persistent and Unspecified use the Logto user ID; Email address uses the user's email; Transient uses a one-time user ID that changes per authentication request. The fuzzer MUST pin the NameID format during a test and MUST NOT compare identities across different NameID formats as if they were expected to be stable.

For I4 collision tests, if Name ID format is set to Transient, repeated logins are expected to produce different identifiers by design. Do NOT flag changing NameID values across sessions as an identity-splitting bug when Transient format is configured.

For I4 email-based collision tests, if Name ID format is set to Email address, the SAML NameID intentionally equals the user's email address. Any account correlation or collision observed under this mode must be interpreted in light of explicit email-based identifier configuration, not as implicit identity collapse.

For I1/I5 tests involving SAML encryption, when 'Encrypt SAML assertion' is enabled, the Service Provider certificate must be configured or the flow is invalid by setup. A failed login without the SP certificate is a test misconfiguration, not evidence of signature or audience enforcement.

Only one SAML signing certificate can be active at a time for a SAML app, and the IdP metadata URL is unavailable when there is no active certificate. Tests that depend on metadata retrieval or signature verification MUST ensure an active certificate exists first.

You cannot delete an active SAML signing certificate; it must be deactivated first, and activating an inactive certificate automatically deactivates the current active certificate. Rotation/coherence tests MUST account for this single-active-certificate model.

For signing-key rotation or I3 coherence tests on Logto-issued SAML assertions, do NOT rotate certificates consecutively without allowing relying parties to update trust. The docs state only one certificate is active and metadata reflects the active certificate; abrupt repeated rotations can invalidate expected trust relationships and create false positives.

Enterprise SSO connectors in Logto link SSO identities to existing accounts if the email matches. For I4 tests involving enterprise SSO or cross-protocol identity merge, email-based linking is documented behavior. The fuzzer MUST distinguish configured email-based account linking from unintended principal collapse.

Only verified email addresses from social or enterprise SSO identity providers can be synced and saved as primary_email. For unverified-email account-linking tests, the fuzzer SHOULD verify whether the upstream email is verified before concluding that email-based linkage occurred improperly.

Logto usernames are case-sensitive, controlled by CASE_SENSITIVE_USERNAME (default true). Case-confusion tests using username MUST account for tenant configuration; 'Admin' and 'admin' may legitimately be distinct identities.

Logto documentation for SAML app integration describes Logto as a SAML Identity Provider (IdP) for external Service Providers, not as a SAML Service Provider consuming upstream SAML assertions. Therefore, do NOT attempt upstream `saml_login`, SAML IdP creation, ACS callback forgery, or SAML assertion mutation tests against Logto in the `saml` profile; those attack patterns target brokers that consume SAML, which is not the documented role here.

For SAML-related testing on Logto, treat the relevant setup surface as application configuration only: create a SAML application and configure ACS URL, SP Entity ID, NameID format, and optional assertion encryption/signing certificate behavior through documented application settings. Do NOT infer undocumented SAML ACS or admin REST endpoints from the UI docs.

`refreshTokenTtlDays` has a documented default sentinel behavior: if not explicitly configured, the default TTL is 14 days. Additionally, refresh-token lifetime is effectively capped by the user session when refresh tokens are issued without `offline_access`: the session TTL is fixed at 14 days and the refresh token becomes invalid when the session expires regardless of its own TTL. Never assume configured refresh token TTL alone controls lifetime.

For I2 freshness tests involving refresh tokens, include `offline_access` in the authorization request if you need the configured refresh token TTL to take full effect. Without `offline_access`, the refresh token is session-bound and expires with the 14-day session even if the application's refresh token TTL is longer.

`rotateRefreshToken` is enabled by default (`true`). For public clients (SPA/native), when enabled, a new refresh token is always issued on refresh. Tests that reuse an old refresh token after a successful refresh may fail by design because rotation invalidates or supersedes the previous token. Capture and use the newest refresh token after each refresh/token exchange step.

Token exchange is disabled by default for applications. Before any `token_exchange` test, the target application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled in application settings; otherwise failures such as 'token exchange is not allowed for this application' are expected setup failures, not security rejections.

For I5 token-exchange audience/scope tests, use `/oidc/token` with `grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange` and pass the target audience in the `resource` parameter. Do not expect a separate `audience` parameter in the documented API; the resource indicator is the documented audience-binding control.

For third-party OIDC/OAuth applications, requesting a non-enabled user profile scope causes an error, while non-enabled API resource scopes and organization scopes are ignored and not granted. Test oracles must distinguish these by-design behaviors from authorization bugs: user-profile-scope rejection is expected, but silently omitted API/org scopes should be checked in the granted token/consent result rather than treated as parser failure.

For I5 organization-permission tests, organization scopes are ignored unless `urn:logto:scope:organizations` is also enabled/requested. A valid test for organization authorization binding MUST include that scope; otherwise missing organization permissions are a setup artifact, not evidence of correct narrowing.

Redirect URI matching in Logto supports wildcard patterns only for SPA and Traditional Web apps, and only in hostname/pathname. Wildcards are not allowed in scheme, port, query, or fragment. Because wildcard redirect URIs are explicitly non-standard and increase attack surface, I1/I3 tests involving redirect URI exactness must account for configured wildcard behavior and should prefer exact redirect URIs unless the test intentionally targets wildcard matching.

Username matching semantics are exact and case-sensitive by default (`CASE_SENSITIVE_USERNAME=true`). For I4 case-confusion tests involving password login or username-based identity lookup, `Admin` and `admin` are distinct usernames by design unless the deployment changes this environment variable. Do not flag separate identities for case variants as a collision bug under default settings.

Enterprise SSO connectors link SSO identities to existing accounts if the email matches. For I4 account-linking tests, same-email merges across enterprise SSO and existing accounts are documented behavior. Only flag a violation when linking occurs on an unverified or attacker-controlled email contrary to documented trust expectations, not when verified email match causes linking.

Only verified email addresses from social or enterprise SSO identity providers are synced into `primaryEmail`, and only verified phone numbers are synced into `primaryPhone`. For I4 unverified-email-account-linking tests, a merge based on unverified upstream email would be suspicious; however, absence of linking when `email_verified=false` is the documented expectation.

SAML application NameID format affects downstream identity representation by design: default 'Persistent' uses Logto user ID, 'Email address' uses email, 'Transient' uses a one-time user ID, and 'Unspecified' currently uses Logto user ID. I4 tests comparing identities across SAML logins must account for configured NameID format; changing NameID output does not imply principal collapse inside Logto.

SAML in Logto is IdP-only for SAML applications in the provided docs. The documented SAML flow is SP-initiated from your application to Logto, then Logto returns a SAML response. Do NOT test Logto as a SAML Service Provider consuming attacker-supplied upstream SAML assertions based on these docs; saml_cert_substitution, saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_issuer_mismatch, saml_spurious_signature, saml_post_binding_unsigned_assertion, saml_no_conditions, saml_wrong_audience, saml_assertion_id_replay, and saml_one_time_use_replay are not supported by the documented surface here and would produce false positives.

For SAML tests on Logto, the relevant trust boundary is downstream: your SP must validate Logto-issued assertions using the active SAML signing certificate from Logto metadata. The docs state only one certificate can be active at a time, the metadata URL is unavailable if there is no active certificate, and activating a new certificate automatically deactivates the current one. Any test that changes certificate state must refresh SP trust from metadata before evaluating results.

Do NOT interpret successful login with a response-level signature or missing assertion-level signature as a Logto broker vulnerability from these docs. Logto is the SAML IdP, not the SAML SP, in the documented SAML app feature. Signature-validation attack patterns against an SP are out of scope for this protocol run.

Enterprise SSO account linking is by design email-based according to the enterprise connectors docs: 'The SSO identities will be linked to existing accounts if the email matches.' For I4 tests involving SAML/enterprise SSO identities, same-email merges are expected behavior, not a collision bug. To test principal binding correctly, vary email as well as upstream identifier.

NameID format materially changes downstream identity semantics for SAML apps. Default is Persistent using the Logto user ID; Email address uses the user's email; Transient generates a one-time identifier that changes with each authentication request; Unspecified currently uses the Logto user ID. For I4 identity-collision tests, do NOT compare identities across different NameID format configurations as if they were the same binding policy.

If the SAML app uses NameID format Transient, repeated sign-ins for the same user are expected to produce different NameID values by design. Do NOT flag this as an I4 principal-binding failure or I2 freshness issue.

For OIDC-based verification and token handling around SAML-integrated applications, Logto issues opaque access tokens when no resource is specified and JWT access tokens when a specific resource or organization is requested. The fuzzer MUST use /oidc/me or /oidc/token/introspection appropriately based on token type; decoding an opaque token as JWT is invalid test setup.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before any token_exchange test, the application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled, otherwise failures are expected and do not indicate an I5 authorization-binding defense.

For token exchange and refresh-token based follow-up tests, refresh token lifetime is session-bound unless offline_access was requested. The docs state that when a refresh token is issued without offline_access, it is bound to a user session with fixed TTL of 14 days regardless of the refresh token TTL setting. Tests that rely on long-lived refresh behavior MUST request offline_access.

Numeric sentinel analysis: refresh token TTL in days has a documented platform default of 14 days and is unavailable for SPA TTL refreshment. Do NOT assume omitted or default TTL means zero lifetime. The provided docs do not document a zero or negative disable sentinel for this parameter.

For OIDC redirect_uri matching in application configuration, wildcard patterns are supported only for SPA and Traditional Web apps, only in hostname and pathname, and are not standard OIDC. For security-sensitive tests, prefer exact redirect URIs; wildcard acceptance is by design when configured and should not be treated as open redirect unless it exceeds the documented wildcard rules.

Applications and third-party apps in Logto are not authorization resources. The docs explicitly state there is no concept of 'signing in to an organization' and applications are not used as resources for access control. Do NOT model SAML app access as organization-bound authentication; organization context is authorization-layer behavior.

For I5 consent and scope tests on third-party/OIDC surfaces used alongside SAML deployments, non-enabled user profile scopes cause an error, while non-enabled API resource scopes and organization scopes are ignored and not shown on the consent screen. The fuzzer MUST distinguish 'error' from 'silently ignored' depending on scope type to avoid false positives.

For I5 tests involving organization permissions, organization scopes are ignored unless urn:logto:scope:organizations is also enabled/requested. A missing organization selector or missing organization scopes without that prerequisite is expected behavior.

Password policy enforcement differs by API surface. End-user flows and Account API enforce current password policy, but Management API PATCH /api/users/{userId}/password is exempt. Do NOT treat successful weak-password provisioning through Management API as a password-policy bypass vulnerability.

Identifier lockout defaults to 100 failed attempts within an hour and 60 minutes lockout. Authentication failures after that threshold may be due to lockout rather than the tested invariant. Include a control using a fresh identifier or manually unblock before concluding on SAML/SSO login behavior.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: Logto Management API uses /api/ prefix. User CRUD: /api/users. SSO connectors: /api/sso-connectors. Applications: /api/applications.
environment_defaults.login_strategy: Logto supports login_with_password via the Experience API handler (the executor handles the multi-step flow). For M2M service login, use login_with_jwt with client_credentials grant.
environment_defaults.app_types: Logto application types: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. Do NOT use TraditionalWeb or WebApp — use 'Traditional'.
environment_defaults.user_fields: create_user accepts ONLY: username, password, name, primaryEmail. Do NOT include primaryPhone (format validation is strict — no + prefix), firstName, lastName, enabled, or other undocumented fields.
